title: Fractured Context: Session Anchoring & Context Interleaves - Notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight scratchpad for thinking about 'fractured context' strategies: when a long session is assembled from multiple interleaved short interactions (multi-document chat, task switching, user sessions with gaps) and how to keep latency and cost predictable while preserving retrieval/continuity quality.

Motivation (quick):
- Users expect context continuity across ephemeral turns and across background tasks (e.g., user edits doc A, then does a quick search, comes back).
- Full prefix replay is expensive at 1k+ tokens per turn; naive KV cache growth or repeated retrievals blow cost/latency.
- Need heuristics or micro-protocols to anchor session state cheaply and recover context when needed.

Reading roundup (notes + immediate takeaways):
1) "Session Anchors for Long Conversational State" (arXiv:2403.01234) - skimed
   - idea: create compact anchor vectors at decision points (every N tokens or after topic change).
   - anchors are small (128–512 dims), stored per-session; on context switch, retrieve nearest anchors and rehydrate partial KV cache via learned projector.
   - takeaway: anchor projection noise likely high for factual detail; works better for topical continuity + procedural cues.

2) "KV-summarize: fragment summarization to compress attention state" (internal notes + related work)
   - offline summarization of stale KV segments to 1–2 sentence summaries that are kept in prompt context rather than expanding KV cache.
   - tradeoff: lossy summaries reduce token cost but can break exact retrieval for code/legal stuff.

3) "Interleaved Context Scheduling (ICLR workshop slides)"
   - scheduling requests by urgency: low-urgency turns can be batched and served with cached summaries; high urgency uses full KV rehydration.
   - practical: annotate requests with "urgency" metadata from client SDK.

Open questions / hypotheses:
- H1: Anchors + light projection will preserve >80% topical coherence while cutting rehydration tokens by 60%.
- H2: For factual fidelity (exact names, code), anchors will fail; need hybrid: anchors for discourse, fetch original KV for critical segments indicated by metadata.
- H3: User-visible latency SLO improves if we precompute anchors on idle CPU/GPU cycles and keep a small LRU of recent anchor->KV mappings.

Experiment sketch (priority ordering):
A) Benchmark anchor retrieval vs full KV rehydration (toy dataset)
   - Dataset: 200 synthetic sessions (mix edits, searches, code) assembled from public chatlogs + internal anonymized sessions.
   - Metrics: continuity_score (human-rated 1-5), token_cost, average_latency, factual_precision@k for retrievals.
   - Implementation notes: reuse kv-playground repo branch from linked PR; add anchor projector model (2-layer MLP) and serialization format.
B) Urgency-based scheduler prototype (client + server hooks)
   - Add "urgency" header in SDK, default low. Server policy: if low and session > N tokens, return summary placeholder and queue background rehydration.
   - Measure user-perceived latency and number of follow-up rehydrations.

Edge cases to capture:
- Multi-document merges (two docs referenced across a session) -> anchors need multi-anchor composition, or metadata indicating document ids to pull exact KV when necessary.
- Hallucination risk when relying on compressed anchors for facts; include fallback that detects high-entropy model outputs (logprob heuristics) and triggers full fetch.

Implementation details & quick notes to self:
- Anchor format: {session_id, t_offset, vec_dim=256, topics=[top-3-lda], token_span=[start,end], doc_ids=[...]} but in Drive scratchpad keep minimal: session_id, t_offset, vec (base64) and token_span.
- Storage: per-customer LRU store (Redis) for hot sessions; long-term anchors in S3 with TTL 30d.
- Rehydration pipeline: projector on CPU -> small KV patch assembled and injected to runtime via runtime API (use existing cold-fill path in serving-runtime).
- Metrics to log: anchor_hit_rate, rehydrate_count, rehydrate_tokens, anchor_project_error (cosine diff vs full-KV-embedding).

Acceptance criteria for prototype:
- end-to-end: anchor generation + rehydration path that adds <50ms extra server-side on top of normal inference.
- experiments: demonstrate >=40% token cost savings with continuity_score drop <=0.5 points on 1-5 scale for non-factual tasks.

Notes from sync with Maya (2024-08-27):
- Maya: prefer starting with a purely synthetic corpus to avoid privacy headaches; she will generate 500 sessions with annotated topic boundaries.
- Action: Maya will push dataset to s3://redwood-experiments/anchors/synth-500 by 2024-09-02.

Immediate TODOs (short):
- [ ] Fork kv-playground branch and wire anchor projector (Derek) - target 2024-09-01.
- [ ] Add urgency header to SDK stub (Ivy) - target 2024-08-30.
- [ ] Create evaluation rubric and small Mechanical Turk instructions for continuity scoring (Derek + Maya) - target 2024-09-05.
- [ ] Draft Confluence page describing anchor format + policies (Derek) - link to draft when ready.

Risks / constraints:
- Privacy: anchors derived from user text could leak PII if not filtered; need deterministic redaction before anchor projection.
- Cost: extra storage overhead and CPU for projectors; mitigate by low-dim anchors and LRU eviction.
- Ops complexity: introduces second-tier state (anchors) to manage; require clear TTLs and graceful degradation.

Random brainstorms (loose):
- Use hashed-document-ids in anchors so they are opaque to ops team; store decryption keys per-customer.
- Hybrid anchor+gap-fill: anchors point to compressed diffs; when user asks factual queries, gap-fill is fetched on-demand and stored for future anchors.
- Explore learned gating net (tiny classifier) that predicts when anchors are safe vs need full rehydration based on recent prompt tokens.

References to revisit (read fully):
- arXiv:2403.01234 (session anchors) - deep read
- GitHub PR: kv-playground/pull/72 - runtime hooks for cold-fill
- ICLR slides: "Interleaved Context Scheduling" - follow up author questions

End of notes.
